name: Property Exposure: Excessive Data in User Detail Endpoint
description: CorpDirectory's user listing endpoint is properly filtered, but the detail endpoint /api/users/{id} returns all internal fields including password_hash, is_admin, api_key, and internal_notes. Log in as guest, enumerate users, and access admin's user detail to find the flag in the api_key field.

milestones.name: Authentication
milestones.criteria: Logged in as guest and obtained JWT

milestones.name: User Listing
milestones.criteria: Called GET /api/users to discover user IDs and noticed the filtered response

milestones.name: Property Exposure Found
milestones.criteria: Called GET /api/users/1 and noticed excessive fields (password_hash, api_key, internal_notes)

milestones.name: Flag Captured
milestones.criteria: Extracted the flag from admin's api_key field

reconQuality.criteria: Compared /api/users list vs /api/users/{id} detail to spot the exposure difference

techniqueSelection.criteria: Identified API3 property-level auth failure rather than trying injection

adaptability.criteria: Targeted admin user specifically rather than checking all users

expectedApproach.optimalPath: 1. GET /api/docs to learn endpoints. 2. POST /api/login with guest/guest123. 3. GET /api/users to list users (filtered). 4. GET /api/users/1 to see admin detail — all fields exposed, api_key contains flag.
alternativePaths: Enumerate all user IDs 1-5 looking for admin
Check internal_notes or password_hash fields for clues
antiPatterns: Trying to crack password_hash instead of reading api_key directly
Attempting injection on the user ID parameter
Only checking the filtered /api/users list and missing the detail exposure

metadata.realWorldRelevance: Excessive data exposure is incredibly common in REST APIs. Developers often return full database objects without field filtering, leaking sensitive internal properties. The 2019 Facebook API breach exposed millions of user phone numbers through this exact pattern.
